scope: Source-proven ownership policy, not proof that every in-place API has a production defect. Unknown ownership and effects remain judgment audit work.
label_definition: MATCH labels describe the supported detector contract. NO_MATCH labels include deliberate abstentions; zero labeled false negatives does not imply complete mutation detection.
shared_analysis: packages/python/src/sarj_python_lint/rules/_copy_on_write.py; cached once per PythonFileContext and backed by the shared project AST index. Application model modules are never imported.

validation.native_self_lint: all 113 Python rules pass on new implementation and tests
validation.cli_behavior: Warnings exit 0 and do not enter blocking baselines.
runtime_evidence: Changed-path replacements preserve original inputs and earlier outputs across repeated calls.
A shallow-copy control demonstrates shared nested identity.
Replacement normalization preserves raw input on validation success and failure.
Discarding a model_copy result leaves the original unchanged.
validation.interactions: SARJ482 owns raw-input mutation in before validators; SARJ401 retains frozen after-validator writes. No same-location duplicate candidate diagnostics were found.

corpus.private_pins: Three verified owner-readable local Git snapshots. Full revisions, content digests, identities, and raw findings remain in the private evaluation boundary.
corpus.snapshot_definition: Git snapshots pin HEAD and current tracked working-tree bytes, including existing uncommitted changes; untracked new regression fixtures are exercised separately by tests.
corpus.selection: All tracked existing Python files in the Git snapshots; all Python source in the already-installed public package copy. No clone, fetch, download, or consumer edit.
corpus.exclusions: The native runner skips oversized files and generated/vendor paths or banners. Maintained tests are included. Counts describe selected inputs, not an assertion that every source has eligible model provenance.
corpus.inspection: Every retained finding was reviewed through anonymized AST structure; 40 input-mutation policy findings and 3 raw-validator mutations, 0 known false positives, 0 duplicates. Nonmatching live locations were not exhaustively reviewed.
refinements: Bound annotation traversal after a recursive public-package type alias crashed the initial candidate.
Exclude import-proven pytest.raises assertions after reviewing four intentionally discarded replacements.
Preserve ownership depth in homogeneous literals and abstain on mixed ownership and keyword-based container overrides.

performance.method: Each corpus and mode runs in a fresh process. Warm medians use three subsequent analyze calls with fresh per-invocation sessions. Cold medians use three fresh-process first calls, with alternating baseline/combined order for the extra repetitions.
performance.cold_caveat: Filesystem caches were not flushed. Timings are local and load-sensitive; initial runs overlapped repository verification. Repeated fresh-process medians resolve the isolated first-run outlier without claiming a controlled OS-cold benchmark.
performance.public_baseline_exclusion: SARJ420 (no-unnecessary-docstring) raises an existing KeyError on a nested owner in the public package. It is excluded symmetrically from that package baseline and combined comparison; private comparisons retain every existing registered rule.
performance.worker_source:
import json, resource, statistics, sys, time
from pathlib import Path
from sarj_python_lint.__main__ import analyze
from sarj_python_lint.rules import REGISTRY
new = {'no-input-model-mutation','no-before-validator-input-mutation','no-unused-copy-result'}
mode=sys.argv[1]
excluded = {'no-unnecessary-docstring'} if sys.argv[2] == 'public' else set()
rules=sorted(new if mode=='candidate-only' else set(REGISTRY)-new-excluded if mode=='baseline' else set(REGISTRY)-excluded)
paths=[Path(path) for path in sys.argv[3:]]
samples=[]
counts=[]
for iteration in range(4):
    started=time.perf_counter()
    findings=analyze(rules, paths)
    samples.append(time.perf_counter()-started)
    counts.append(len(findings))
print(json.dumps({'mode':mode,'process_cold_seconds':samples[0],'warm_seconds':samples[1:],
                 'warm_median_seconds':statistics.median(samples[1:]),'peak_memory_bytes':resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss,
                 'findings_per_run':counts,'rules':len(rules),'excluded_rules':sorted(excluded),'python':sys.version.split()[0]}))
performance.cold_worker_adjustment: For each additional cold sample, use range(1) and omit the warm median; execute the same mode and selected files in a new interpreter.

limitations: Offline syntax-only evaluation; no application ownership or receiver type proof.
Parameter alias writes and nested sharing remain undetected.
Widening also reports fresh builders and stateful receiver operations.
No global ban on mutation, no readonly-parameter mandate, no frozen-model mandate, and no universal discarded-call rule.
Ambiguous control flow, captured closures, opaque calls, custom copy hooks, dynamic update mappings, and deep-copy provenance abstain.
Recursive annotation traversal is bounded; constructor argument sharing through custom validation is not propagated.
Shallow copies and readonly/frozen outer contracts do not provide deep immutability.
model_copy(update=...) does not validate; replacement values must satisfy the complete model contract, including cross-field invariants.
Serialization round trips are not a universal replacement strategy.
promotion: Retain warnings without autofix through at least one warning release and broader ownership/adoption review before a separate error-promotion change.

reproduction.performance: Run the included worker with <mode> <visibility> <selected-relative-paths...> from each pinned corpus root using the standards interpreter. Modes: baseline (registry minus candidates), combined (full registry), candidate-only. Take the first 250 sorted pinned paths, or all when fewer; repeat first calls in fresh processes and three subsequent analyze calls for warm medians.
